tone_statements.citation: Sonkoue Kamdem, Eliane. 2019. Mengaka tense-aspect system. Nordic Journal of African Studies 28(3): 1-17. doi:10.53228/njas.v28i3.455
tone_statements.quote: Verb roots in Mengaka are mainly monosyllabic, with one of the following two major syllable structures: CV, for example, fú ‘read’, mè ‘finish’ and CVC, for example, ɣə̀p ‘distribute’, fáʔ ‘cultivate’. Two classes of verb roots may be distinguished in Mengaka on the basis of their lexical tones: high and low tone verb roots. [...] The Hodiernal Past is indicated by a tone alternation on the verb. More precisely, the lexical tone of the only or last vowel of the verb is realised as a low high tone at the level of the surface structure.
tone_statements.locator: p. 3 (sec. 2, 'Position 5') and p. 7; see also Table 1 p. 3, Table 2 pp. 6-7, sec. 4.3 p. 9 (Near Past HL tone on subject), sec. 4.10 p. 13 (Future H tone)
tone_statements.summary: Lexical tone on verb roots with two classes (H vs L) and productive grammatical tone: TAM categories marked by LH, HL and H tonal alternations on the verb or the subject and by an underlying H-toned imperfective suffix; full toneme inventory (levels/contours, noun tone, downstep) not stated.

sources.note: Morphosyntactic description with first-hand tonal data: verb roots fall into two lexical tone classes (high vs low); the nasal verb prefix 'always bears a high tone'; the imperfective suffix is an underlying high tone realised by vowel lengthening/copying, merging with a low root into a LH contour (Table 1: fì + í -> [fǐː], ɣə̀p + ə́ -> [ɣə̀bə́]); tense is partly marked by tonal alternation -- Hodiernal Past = LH tone on the verb's last vowel (neutralising the H/L verb contrast), Near Past = HL tone on the last vowel of the subject pronoun/noun, Future = H tone on the verb plus ní/dɛ́ (Table…
